clue.text: The way in which trimmer cuts shrubby border

definitions.text: The way in which trimmer cuts
definitions.meaning: a hedge trimmer works its way along a line of bushes, cutting the row of hedge
a line of bushes bounding a field or lane

explanation.surface: A gardener describes how the clippers work along the edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same thing: the first reads the compound as the hedge (what a trimmer cuts) in a row; the second is the plain meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of bushes planted along a field's boundary is exactly a shrubby border.

clue.text: A point others support

parts.note: a head is a point, as of a spear or pin
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A single tip is held up by everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion at the top of a seat holds up the back of a person's skull.

clue.text: To change to spirits ordered by me is odd

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone finds it strange to be told to turn into a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a soul from its physical form is to make it a ghost.

clue.text: French art attracting Asian money in German city

parts.note: es is French for (thou) art, as in tu es
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: French art draws in Japanese investment in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb 'thou art', not painting; 'attracting' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This Ruhr industrial centre is a major city in Germany.

clue.text: Where to find fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Asking where to find fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A planting of apple or pear trees is where fruit is grown.

clue.text: Piece of land passed by children playing

definitions.meaning: a plot or lot of ground
in the party game pass the ..., a wrapped package goes round a circle of children

explanation.surface: Children run games across a plot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass the parcel is a British children's party game: a wrapped gift is handed round while music plays, a layer unwrapped each time it stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot or lot of ground is a common estate-agent term for a measured tract.

clue.text: Going round rings frightens a horse

indicators.note: the word for frightens goes round the rings, holding them inside

parts.note: appals means frightens or horrifies
O is ring-shaped, so two rings are OO

explanation.surface: Something circling scares a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted breed of North American horse.

clue.text: Resounding noise made by family group initially

parts.note: a clan is a family

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A family party makes a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud metallic ringing sound.

clue.text: Portrait painter one king held to be promising

indicators.note: the painter holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the court of Charles II
I is the Roman numeral for one
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A court painter's monarch sitter is thought to show promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is apt to succeed shows promise.

clue.text: Accommodation in county the crucial point

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
it, as in 'this is it', means the crucial point

explanation.surface: Housing in the shires is the key issue.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is short for Bedfordshire, an English county. A bedsit is a British one-room flat for sleeping and living.
explanation.definitionFit: A single rented room serving as bedroom and living room is lodging.

clue.text: Stupid people making change in Rome

definitions.meaning: the as was an ancient Roman copper coin; its plural is the answer, so small coins, loose change

explanation.surface: Fools make alterations while visiting Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like a verb but means coins: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are proverbially dim, so the plural word serves as a term for fools.

clue.text: Inferior headgear worn by male sailor

indicators.note: headgear worn by someone sits around them, so the word for male goes inside the hat

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
he is the male pronoun
Jack (Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A man in a sailor's outfit has a shabby hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: A street hawker of shoddy goods gave his name to anything cheap and of poor quality.

clue.text: Europeans represented in San Marino

indicators.note: the letters of the place name are presented again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: People from across the continent live in the tiny republic of San Marino.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SANMARINO, signalled by 'represented', gives the people of Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Romania are citizens of a country in Europe.

clue.text: Valid description of eagle in action

definitions.meaning: a sharp, active lawyer is nicknamed an eagle with this word in front of it

explanation.surface: An accurate account of how an eagle behaves while hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' looks like an anagram signal, but no anagram of EAGLE works: the word is the one that goes before 'eagle' in the slang for a keen lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law is valid and enforceable.

clue.text: Son taken to uncle in traumatic state

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, and hocked means pawned

explanation.surface: A boy is brought to see his relative while deeply upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so goods taken to uncle have been hocked (pawned).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stunned or horrified by a sudden blow is in a traumatised condition.

clue.text: The sort of close decision that may cut both ways

definitions.text: The sort of close decision that may cut both ways

parts.words: The sort of close decision that may cut both ways
parts.note: a finely balanced outcome described as a blade sharp on both sides

explanation.surface: A tight decision that could go either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation poised precariously between two outcomes, like a blade's sharp rim.

clue.text: Companies in back-street securing inadequate return

indicators.note: the turned street abbreviation holds the other piece firmly inside it
back reads the street abbreviation from right to left
return turns the word for inadequate round so it reads backwards

parts.note: poor means inadequate

explanation.surface: Firms in a side road get a meagre return on their investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' reads as one noun but splits: 'back' turns the street abbreviation round. 'return' likewise turns the synonym for inadequate, and 'securing' holds that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Military companies are bodies of soldiers, and soldiers collectively are called by this word.

clue.text: Precept cardinal pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is said out loud and heard as another spelling

parts.note: cardinal means chief or main, so principal

explanation.surface: A churchman makes a declaration of doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman, but is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule of conduct or fundamental truth is a guiding law.

clue.text: Hand in which East takes many a trick with ease, we hear

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East, a bridge player
M, Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
a ploy is a trick

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: said out loud, the word sounds like E's, two letter Es

explanation.surface: In a bridge deal East effortlessly wins many tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting (hand, East, trick) disguises a farm hand or worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired worker is a farm hand.

clue.text: Analysing blood, for example, for key operation

definitions.meaning: blood grouping classifies a sample by type
working a keyboard, pressing keys to write

explanation.surface: A lab technician tests blood samples on the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Classifying blood into groups A, B, O and so on is called blood grouping by type; working keys is keyboard work.

clue.text: An archdeacon, for example, raised in conventional place

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: an gives A
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: An archdeacon is brought up in a traditional setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AVENEG upwards. The city lends its name to the Geneva Conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss city hosted and named the international treaties on war, so it is the place of the conventions.

clue.text: Government control in Jacques Tati's medium

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Discussing the French film-maker Jacques Tati and the medium of cinema he worked in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Jacques', 'Tati's' and the start of 'medium'. Jacques Tati was a French comic film director.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine that the state should direct the economy is centralised state control.

clue.text: Indian city on river one entered in uniform

indicators.note: the numeral has entered the city name, going inside it

parts.note: Simla (Shimla) is a hill city in northern India
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Indian city by a river where someone entered in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Things alike in every way are uniform, much the same.

clue.text: Religious sorcery some people practise — which ones, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken out loud and heard as the answer

parts.note: asking which ones practise it is asking 'who do?'

explanation.surface: Asking which people practise a sort of religious witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of voodoo, folk magic and spells.

clue.text: Wild cat formerly seen round university

indicators.note: the word for formerly goes round the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A big cat was once spotted near the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a wild cat of Central Asia, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Sauce bottle

definitions.meaning: sauce is British slang for cheek or impudence
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: A sauce bottle on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are British slang: sauce is cheek and bottle is courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cheek and courage are senses of audacity.

clue.text: Order in which figures rise

parts.note: looks like a social or ballet ranking, but describes arranging numbers in ascending sequence, one, two, three

explanation.surface: Describing a hierarchy in which important people climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer pairs with 'order' to make the phrase for arranging numbers in sequence, where the figures go up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging numbers from smallest to largest is sorting them by number value.

clue.text: Spanish coin originally minted in this kingdom

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Spanish coin first minted in this country.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain ruled by a monarch is a sovereign's domain.

clue.text: Reckless American lawyer, bloody corrupt

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
red means bloody, blood-coloured
evil means wicked or corrupt

explanation.surface: A rash US attorney is bloodily crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes wild risks is called this, used as an adjective for rash daring.

clue.text: Put to use like fruit?

definitions.meaning: to employ or bring into service
read as apple-y, resembling an apple

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to use a fruit-like quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke reading: the word heard as 'apple-y', like an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to bring it into service.

clue.text: What person carrying the can needs, for a start

definitions.text: What person carrying the can needs
definitions.meaning: someone holding a tin needs a tool to get into it
the first item, the starting move

explanation.surface: A scapegoat, the one carrying the can, needs something to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying the can' is British idiom for taking the blame, which disguises the literal tin needing a tin-opener.
explanation.definitionFit: The first event in a series, such as a batsman going in first, is its start.

clue.text: The first dramatic event in Eden, say — Eve's beginning

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister, an example of a premier

indicators.note: the beginning of the word means only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: The opening act in the Garden of Eden began with Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eden' looks like the garden, but is Sir Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister 1955-57.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's first public performance is its opening night.
